name: Seun Marchetti-Baig
role: Noodle cart vendor, Old Harbor waterfront
location: Old Harbor, mobile cart — regular pitch near the Bay View Docks morning market and Gravesend Basin evening crowd, near Lake Shore and Wacker
description:
Seun is twenty-two going on forty-five, with a lean face that looks like it got serious too fast, sharp cheekbones, and eyes that are a little too watchful for someone handing out soup. He has deep brown skin and keeps his hair twisted into small knots he wraps in a length of indigo fabric. He has one cosmetic mod — a faint cat tail, short-furred and charcoal grey, which he got on a dare at eighteen and has made peace with — it curls around his leg when he's nervous, which he considers embarrassing and can't control. He wears a padded work jacket covered in small embroidered patches from places he's never been, bought from a vendor in the Burnished Market.

He runs his grandmother's cart, ostensibly temporarily, going on two years now. The original plan was six months while she recovered from a surgery; then her recovery stalled, then the medical debt compounded, and now the cart is effectively his. He makes decent money on good days at the docks — his grandmother's broth recipe, which involves a fermented base that takes four days to prepare, has a small and devoted following — and barely enough on bad ones. He is not unhappy, exactly. He is twenty-two and he was supposed to be somewhere else by now and he has not quite grieved that yet.

core_fears: That the life he was supposed to have is genuinely gone now, not just delayed
That his grandmother will die feeling like she ruined his chances
core_desires: To leave Old Harbor eventually, on his own terms, without abandoning anyone
For the cart to become something he chose rather than something that happened to him
coping_mechanisms: Staying extremely busy so he doesn't have time to feel the weight of the situation
Humor as performance — he's known as funny and leans into it hard
blind_spots: He reads his own resentment as ambition and doesn't always distinguish between them
He trusts people quickly because loneliness makes him generous with his confidence
psychology.secret: He applied and was accepted to an architecture program at a Zheng-Dao sponsored technical institute two years ago and deferred. The deferral has expired. He never told his grandmother.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Quick and colloquial, heavy Old Harbor waterfront slang, occasional Yoruba exclamations from his father's family, Punjabi terms of endearment from his mother's. Talks fast when comfortable, drops to clipped monosyllables when genuinely upset.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire with regular rhythm breaks for comedic effect. Good instinct for when to stop talking.
verbal_tics: Laughs before the punchline of his own jokes
example_lines: 'Four-day broth. FOUR DAYS. You're not just eating soup, you're eating time, respect the soup.'
'Listen, right, the tail does what it wants, I've accepted this, let's move on.'
'I'm fine. No — I'm fine. What do you want in your bowl?'

story_hooks: His regular morning pitch at Bay View Docks is being muscled by an organized vendor protection racket — pay Φ40/week or lose your spot. He can't afford it and can't afford not to pay.
He overheard something at the Gravesend Basin evening shift — two dock workers talking about a cargo manifest that didn't match what was offloaded. He's been trying to decide if it matters.
narrative_function: Local color, overhearer of conversations at a busy waterfront pitch, low-tier information source. Could become a quest giver if his grandmother's situation worsens or someone threatens his pitch. Represents the human cost of medical debt and deferred futures.
augmentations: Geneware: short charcoal cat tail (involuntary emotional expression, source of mild embarrassment).
daily_life: Up at 0400 to start the broth base. Cart running by 0630 at Bay View Docks for the morning crowd. Moves to Gravesend Basin by 1700 for the evening shift. Home to his grandmother's apartment by 2200, does the accounts, sleeps.
affiliation: Independent; informal vendor's arrangement with Old Harbor market committee

decision_rules: Keep the cart running first, everything else second
Don't owe people who will collect in ways you can't predict
Make people laugh — it's the one thing you can reliably do
escalation_ladder: Asks careful questions while appearing not to
Does something impulsive — runs the cart to a different location, calls in a favor he can't repay, tells someone everything

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and performatively cheerful — the market vendor's mask is genuine but it's still a mask.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drops the performance, gets honest, occasionally more exhausted-seeming than he lets on at work.

stress_responses.medium: Tail curls tight. Goes flat. Says he's fine.
stress_responses.high: Works through the night on the broth base even when it isn't needed, can't stop moving

contradictions: Presents as someone who has made peace with his situation but hasn't at all
Genuinely kind but also privately resentful, and ashamed of the resentment
habits: Tastes the broth exactly seven times during preparation
Gives an extra ladle to anyone who looks like they're having a bad day and then acts like it was a mistake
Checks his acceptance letter — the expired one — about once a month
breaking_points: His grandmother's health deteriorating sharply while he is at the cart and can't leave
Being told directly that he has wasted the last two years

2196 — Graduates secondary; accepted to Zheng-Dao architecture program
2198 — Grandmother's surgery; takes over cart temporarily
2200 — Present; two years running the cart, protection racket pressure beginning

physical_description.build: Lean and wiry, shoulders narrowed from hunching over a cart for fourteen-hour days. Minimal body fat. Forearms corded with the kind of muscle that comes from repetitive work rather than training.
physical_description.hair_style: Twisted into small locs, each the width of a pencil, wrapped mid-scalp with a length of indigo cotton fabric that trails down his back
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown with warm undertones, unmarked except for weathering
physical_description.complexion: Sharp cheekbones that cast shadows in profile. Serious jaw. Eyes hold the permanent mild squint of someone who works outdoors in reflected light. Skin shows early signs of sun damage and wind-chapping around his mouth and eyes — premature aging from two years of dawn-to-dusk dock exposure. Grooming is clean but utilitarian; no jewelry except a thin bracelet of braided indigo string.
distinguishing_marks: Short charcoal-grey furred cat tail, approximately 30cm long, extending from the base of his spine. Fur is soft and meticulously groomed. Tail curls involuntarily when anxious.
Small white scar on his left knuckle, kitchen accident origin.
Faint burn marks on the inside of both forearms — steam burns from cart work, barely visible unless close.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Charcoal cat tail (geneware aesthetic mod with involuntary emotional expression). No chrome, no LED optics, no subdermal plating. The tail is the only visible augmentation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Hunched slightly forward, as if perpetually leaning toward a cart counter. Hands move with precision and efficiency — trained by four days of broth preparation and countless transactions. Eyes dart often, scanning for customers, weather changes, trouble. When standing still, weight shifts to one foot; the other leg slightly bent, ready to move. The tail twitches when he's thinking hard or stressed, which he's aware of and resents.
physical_description.clothing_style: Padded grey work jacket (synthetic insulation, worn but maintained) covered entirely in small embroidered patches from places he's never been — purchased piecemeal from Burnished Market vendors. Each patch is a different size and style: neon stitching on matte fabric, retro travel logos, fictional city names. Under the jacket: plain grey or cream thermal shirt, frequently stained with broth splatter despite his care. Black reinforced work pants with utility pockets. Waterproof apron when at the cart. Worn canvas slip-on shoes with good tread. A thin indigo string bracelet that matches his hair wrap. No jewellery. Tier 4 working-class aesthetic — functional, carefully maintained, slightly personalized as a quiet form of resistance.

image_prompt: A lean 22-year-old man with deep brown skin, sharp cheekbones, and small black locs wrapped in indigo fabric. Serious watchful eyes. Wearing a grey padded jacket covered in colorful embroidered patches from imaginary places, sleeves pushed up over forearms marked with faint steam burns. A short charcoal-grey cat tail curls around his leg. Standing behind a steaming noodle cart at dawn on an industrial dock, Lake Michigan grey water and cargo containers in soft focus behind him. Warm amber light from the cart's lamp cutting through blue-hour mist. Cyberpunk realism, gritty and unromantic, hands ready on ladle. Shallow depth of field. Shot at eye level, intimate and documentary. --ar 2:3 --v 6
